title: Quantification of drug-induced fractional killing using high-throughput microscopy
protocol: Seed mKate2+ cells for treatment.
Trpsinize, quench, and count mKate2+ cells.
Resuspend cells in culture media at the density determined from pilot experiments.
Seed cells in appropriate tissue culture vessel.
Centrifuge seeded cells at 55 × g for 5 seconds.
Place seeded plate in a tissue culture incubator to allow cell adherence for 18-24 hours.
Add SYTOX Green dye to culture medium at a concentration of 20 nM.
Prepare treatment media by diluting compounds of interest in SYTOX Green-containing medium.
Perform serial dilutions of compounds if testing multiple doses is desired.
Include vehicle control treatments as appropriate.
Invert the seeded plate and flick sharply into a basin to remove seeding medium.
Replace with 200 μL of treatment medium without allowing wells to dry completely.
Begin Incucyte imaging of the plate.
Place the plate in an open slot of the Incucyte instrument.
Ensure that the plate is seated securely and level along all edges.
Select the plate definition for the specific vessel from the list of preset options in Incucyte Zoom software.
Add the plate to the repeating scan schedule to scan once every 4 hours.
Complete the Incucyte experiment and obtain raw counts for analysis.
Stop the experiment at the endpoint determined in pilot experiments.
Run analysis of collected images using a cell line-optimized analyzer.
Export time course data for each treatment condition for three object count parameters: SYTOX Green+ objects per mm², mKate2+ objects per mm², and overlap objects per mm².
Pause to allow immediate further analysis or electronic storage until later time.
Process raw object counts to calculate cell death kinetic parameters.
Convert raw counts to a lethal fraction (LF) metric.
Curve fit LF values over the course of an experiment.
Calculate death onset (DO) and death rate (DR) parameters from curve fitting.
Use DR values to quantify the rate of drug-induced fractional killing (FK).
Compare parameter values between diverse conditions acquired in parallel.
Calculate LF for each time point in each experimental condition.
Plot LF data over time using GraphPad Prism software.
Fit a one phase association curve to the LF data.
This curve includes a plateau phase and an exponential phase according to the LED model.
In GraphPad Prism, select “Nonlinear regression (curve fit)” from the XY analyses category.
Select “Plateau followed by one phase association” under the “Exponential” category in the “Model” tab.
Change the Constraint Type for X0 (corresponding to DR) to “No constraint.”
Click “OK” to perform the curve-fitting analysis.
Extract kinetic parameters from fitted curve.
Confirm a successful curve fit in the Results sheet corresponding to the LF data table.
Check if nonlinear regression analysis determined parameters for the curve; label column as “Ambiguous” and do not use 95% CI values if unsuccessful.
Determine DR, DO, baseline LF preceding DO, and LF at conclusion of experiment from kinetic parameters.
